- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast moderately.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 5–10% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model fails to adjust; check for mean reversion and reduce forecast slope accordingly.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to recent volatility; smooth out extremes by applying a 3-day moving average filter to forecast path.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral or bearish), model tends to underperform; add a 2–3% upward bias to forecast.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% for the first 5 days of the horizon.
